text: Carlos Gardel is a station on Line B of the Buenos Aires Underground. It is located in the Balvanera barrio at the intersection of Avenida Corrientes and Calle Agüero and was opened on 17 October 1930 as part of the inaugural section of the line between Federico Lacroze and Callao. The station runs beneath the Abasto de Buenos Aires, one of the city's most prominent landmarks, and features an underground connection that allows access to the shopping centre without exiting to street level. Initially named Agüero after the road it crosses, the station was later renamed Carlos Gardel in honor of the famous tango singer, who was known as "El Morocho del Abasto" (The Brunette boy from Abasto).
